faqs.q: What is the average teacher salary in Victoria?
faqs.a: According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, the average full-time adult ordinary time earnings in Victoria were $2,041.10 per week as of May 2026. This is an average figure, not a median or a specific award rate. Actual teacher salaries vary by experience, classification, and school sector.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual salary before tax and super.

faqs.q: Does the National Minimum Wage apply to teachers?
faqs.a: No, teachers are covered by specific awards or enterprise agreements, such as the Victorian Government Schools Agreement. The National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026) is the minimum for award-free employees. Teachers generally earn above this.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Teacher Salary in Victoria

If you're looking at a **teacher salary vic** offer or trying to convert an hourly rate into annual figures, you've come to the right place. Whether you're a graduate teacher, a relief teacher, or considering a move to the Victorian education system, knowing how to calculate your gross annual pay, fortnightly earnings, tax, and superannuation is essential. This guide uses the latest Fair Work and Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) data to help you make sense of the numbers.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The standard way to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week (the standard full-time week under the National Employment Standards), the formula becomes:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your hourly rate is $40, your annual gross pay would be $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040. This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It's a starting point for comparing job offers or understanding your potential earnings.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Breakdown

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the example above:

- Weekly pay: $40 × 38 = $1,520
- Fortnightly pay: $1,520 × 2 = $3,040

Knowing your fortnightly figure helps with budgeting and comparing to salary packages that are quoted fortnightly.

### Tax and Super: What Comes Off and What's Added

Your gross annual pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies progressive tax rates and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 income year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The calculator on our [timesheet](/) uses the single reduction thresholds from 2025–26 as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide.

Superannuation is paid on top of your salary. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual gross is $80,000, your employer must contribute an additional $9,600 into your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay—it's an extra benefit.

### Teacher Salary in Victoria: What the Data Says

According to the ABS Average Weekly Earnings survey for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings in Victoria were $2,041.10 per week. This is an average across all full-time employees in Victoria, not a median or a specific figure for teachers. However, it gives a useful benchmark. Using the 38-hour week assumption, that weekly figure translates to an annual gross of approximately $106,137.

It's important to note that actual **teacher salary vic** rates depend on your classification (graduate, experienced, leading teacher), the school sector (government, Catholic, independent), and any applicable enterprise agreement. The Victorian Government Schools Agreement, for example, sets out pay scales that are generally higher than the National Minimum Wage. For the most accurate figures, refer to your specific award or agreement. Our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides more context on how averages differ from job-specific medians.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage, set by the Fair Work Commission, is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour.

However, most teachers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. For example, a graduate teacher in Victoria under the government schools agreement earns well above the National Minimum Wage. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page on our site explains the difference between the national floor and award rates.

If you work casually as a teacher, you may be entitled to the 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. Our [timesheet](/) includes a checkbox to add casual loading—never enter a rate that already includes the loading; the tool adds it for you. For more on casual pay, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guide.

### Putting It All Together: An Example

Let's say you're a graduate teacher in Victoria with an hourly rate of $45 (based on the average for early-career teachers under the Victorian agreement). Assuming 38 hours per week:

- Annual gross: $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920
- Fortnightly gross: ($45 × 38) × 2 = $3,420
- Estimated tax (using 2026–27 rates): approximately $18,667 (including Medicare)
- Estimated take-home pay: around $70,253 per year
- Super (12% on top): $10,670.40

Remember, this is an estimate. Your actual tax may vary if you have deductions, HELP debt, or the Medicare levy surcharge. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page offers more detail on net income calculations.

### Key Takeaways

- Use the formula **hourly rate × hours per week × 52** to estimate annual gross pay. Assume 38 hours for full-time unless your contract says otherwise.
- Fortnightly pay is weekly pay × 2.
- Super is paid on top at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base.
- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour (from 1 July 2026), but teachers are covered by higher award rates.
- The ABS average full-time weekly earnings in Victoria is $2,041.10—an average, not a median for teachers.
- Use our [reference tables](/data) for more detailed tax and super figures, and check the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for salary sacrifice options.

Whether you're negotiating a new role or just curious about your **teacher salary vic**, this guide gives you the tools to convert hourly rates into meaningful annual, fortnightly, and take-home figures. Always verify with your employer or the Fair Work Ombudsman for your specific situation.
